A-SW1 originally ran at the default STP priority (32768) for VLAN10, correctly deferring root status to D-SW1 (priority 24586).

No VTP domain name was configured on any switch beforehand, so no synchronization occurred. The moment a common domain name ("CORPNET") was applied to all four switches, VTP's rule — trust the highest revision number as authoritative, regardless of which database is actually current — caused every other switch in the domain to accept A-SW1's outdated VLAN database, silently overwriting VLAN 30's name everywhere. This is the textbook "rogue switch with stale config wipes the network" VTP failure mode: the fault isn't a typo or a broken link, it's a switch that was technically correctly configured for its own (outdated) context, whose mere reconnection to the domain retroactively corrupts every other switch, with no warning, confirmation prompt, or error logged anywhere.
